detail.longDescription: Four months ago, I got curious about building my own programming language. All I wanted was for it to be written in Rust and compiled to native code. My initial goal was simply to print "Hello World" in the terminal. I pulled it off, and from there, I kept adding more features. I knew absolutely nothing about compilers when I started. Along the way, I discovered a whole new world of concepts: parsing, semantic analysis, AST, ASan, LSan, UB, LLVM, IR, drop glue, double free, LSP, and so on. Today, I feel like I know maybe 5% of it. Now it's time to fix all the bugs that will inevitably show up. So I created Tyrus: TypeScript syntax. Rust semantics. What is already implemented: - Lexer, parser, and AST - Type checker with inference and generics - Borrow checker with NLL - LLVM codegen - REPL with JIT - Async functions, async/await, and task management - Arrays, tuples, Map, Set, and collection methods - Option/Result, comptime, defer/errdefer, exhaustive pattern matching, and pipe operator - Validator Decorations - Automated tests and a CLI to create, check, build, run, and watch projects - LSP for VS Code, Neovim, Zed, Kate, and IntelliJ/WebStorm - WASM playground - Native modules: fs, os, net, http, process, temporal, crypto, algorithm, archive, compress, db, encoding, stream, task, and others https://tyruslang.org What feature would you implement if you were building your own programming language?
